chunks.text: Randomly masking a series or computing series-wise similarity tends to distort or ignore the temporal correlations that make time series meaningful. This paper introduces TimeSiam, a simple but effective self-supervised framework built on Siamese networks.

chunks.text: Here is how TimeSiam works. From a single time series it randomly samples two windows: a past subseries and a current subseries, together called Siamese subseries. The current window is lightly corrupted with a simple augmentation such as masking.

chunks.text: Two shared-weight Siamese encoders process the past and current windows, and a decoder with cross-attention reconstructs the masked current series using the past observation as context. That single design choice, reconstructing the current from the past, forces the model to internalize how distant moments in a series relate.
